clue.text: Smelling of particular type of wine before start of orthodox period of fasting

parts.note: red is a type of wine

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of orthodox
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A wine buff notices a vintage's aroma just before giving it up for Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smelling of' is the whole phrase the answer replaces, but 'of' also has to serve as the joint into the wordplay, so the definition is just 'Smelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means fragrant or giving off a strong scent, as in a room redolent of roses.

clue.text: Have a quick look up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word must read the same going up the column as coming down it

parts.note: a short glance, which spelt in either direction is the same

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a fast glance up and down at a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' sounds like the direction of the glance; it actually says the answer reads the same both ways in its column.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to glance briefly or furtively, often through a gap.

clue.text: Vehicle used by boy overturned by one damaging property

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, overturning something turns it upside down so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad borrows a van and tips it over, and gets branded a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who wilfully destroys or damages property.

clue.text: Beg to live, going to diocese supported by church

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a see is a bishop's diocese
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A cleric pleads to stay alive while being posted to a diocese with church backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts the church piece underneath, i.e. at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or entreat urgently, the same as to beg.

clue.text: Male with Dutch tool for gathering up plant

parts.note: a man is a male
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
a rake gathers up leaves or hay

explanation.surface: A man uses a Dutch garden implement to collect up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch tool' looks like one item, such as a Dutch hoe, but Dutch only supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean plant of the nightshade family with a forked root, famous in folklore.

clue.text: Disturbed Derby's second rider with odds fix

indicators.note: a fix is a rigged outcome, so these letters are rigged into a new order
second points to the letter in position two of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the letter in position two of Derby
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey in the Derby is upset to find the betting odds rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, which gives the racing picture; here it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disordered is in disarray or confused, just as something disturbed has been thrown out of order.

clue.text: Choose the French condiment

parts.note: to pick is to choose
le is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A diner is told to select the French sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is a preserved relish served with food, a common condiment.

clue.text: Wise man hiding jug in waste disposal system

indicators.note: to hide something you keep it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A wise old man has stashed a jug down the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the network of sewers that carries away waste water and sewage.

clue.text: Proof of innocence given by setter during arrangement of bail

indicators.note: something happening during another thing sits inside it
an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A defendant offers evidence of innocence while bail terms are being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the person writing the clue, so 'setter' gives I, placed inside the reordered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim, backed by evidence, that the accused was elsewhere when a crime took place.

clue.text: With which to wash small old age pensioner?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
OAP is the British abbreviation for old age pensioner

explanation.surface: It wonders what a little elderly person might be bathed with.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP (old age pensioner) is a British term for a retired person drawing a state pension.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is the cleansing substance people use when they wash.

clue.text: Republican in state where progress is impossible with Southern hairstyle

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a deadlock is a standstill where neither side can advance
R is the abbreviation for Republican
S is the abbreviation for Southern

explanation.surface: A Republican stuck in a stalemated Southern state turns out to be about hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a US state alongside Republican and Southern, but it means a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a hairstyle of long matted or twisted ropes of hair.

clue.text: With this type of remedy get better taking peeled rhubarb?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the kind of remedy

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: to heal is to recover, to get better

indicators.note: here peeling leaves only the skin-like ends of the word, keeping its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of rhubarb

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether eating rhubarb with its skin removed will cure them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' normally means removing the outer letters; here it is used loosely, with only the outer letters of rhubarb kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal remedy is a medicine made from plants, and rhubarb has long been used in such medicines.

clue.text: British weather event leads to sudden inspiration

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a rainstorm is a weather event

explanation.surface: A typical British downpour gives someone a sudden bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden clever idea, a flash of insight.

clue.text: Note name given to Manchester's last dealer in a specified trade

parts.note: C is a musical note
a handle is slang for a name

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Manchester

explanation.surface: A Manchester merchant is handed a note bearing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in particular goods, such as candles or ship supplies (a ship's chandler).

clue.text: Composer's special technique rejected by American soprano

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: an art is a skill or technique
US is short for American
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: An American soprano turns down a composer's distinctive method.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'technique' is turned round; 'special' gives its letter in front of it. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss is the surname of several composers, notably Johann Strauss II and Richard Strauss.

clue.text: Erotic dancer sees tourist after the end of gyrations

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter of gyrations
a tripper is a day tourist

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker watches an exotic dancer once her gyrations have finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the tourist after the letter; tripper is British for a day-tripper or sightseer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is a performer who removes clothing in an erotic dance.

clue.text: Row of houses with dog running round the Queen

indicators.note: running round something encircles it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or trace them
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen

explanation.surface: A dog runs circles round the Queen outside a row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb, meaning to follow or track, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses joined together in a continuous line, common in Britain.

clue.text: Actors with neat arrangement for half an instrument

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a production

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company of actors works out a tidy musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Castanets come as a pair of clicking shells, so a single one is half the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A castanet is one of the pair of shell-shaped wooden clappers played together as one instrument.

clue.text: Renewed performance from competitor swallowing extra Viagra, primarily

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside

parts.note: a rival is a competitor

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of extra and Viagra

explanation.surface: A competitor's comeback performance owes something to an extra dose of Viagra.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival is a new production of an old play or show, a performance staged again.

clue.text: Alternative source of milk for ewe's runt organised

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A farmer arranges a substitute milk supply for a ewe's weakest lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman who breastfeeds another's baby, replacing the mother's milk.

clue.text: Fluffed lines — time to sign up

indicators.note: fluffed means botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor who forgets his lines decides it is time to join the army instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to enrol or sign up, especially for military service.

clue.text: Way for holy person to be humble

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A route to sainthood is said to be through humility.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest means unassuming about one's achievements, the same as humble.

clue.text: Mother given first bit of garden obtained grub

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of garden
got means obtained

explanation.surface: Mum goes out to the garden and comes back with something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' suggests food, as in the surface, but here it means a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the larva of a fly, a grub.

clue.text: Creature offering advice to punters, dumping stuff illegally

parts.note: a fly is a creature
tipping horses means advising gamblers which to back

explanation.surface: A tipster creature advises gamblers while illegally dumping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Punters are gamblers; fly-tipping is the British term for illegally dumping rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-tipping is the illegal disposal of waste on land not licensed to receive it.

clue.text: Originally, colonialists swindled African republic

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of colonialists
to have someone is to swindle them, as in 'I've been had'

explanation.surface: Colonial powers once cheated an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked republic in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Musical animals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Andrew Lloyd Webber stage show

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as animals that are musical, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is the long-running Lloyd Webber show, and cats are also feline pets.

clue.text: Insect jumping from police officer's cloth

indicators.note: something jumping from a place leaves it, so those letters drop out

parts.note: a sergeant is a police rank
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug hops off a policeman's uniform fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twilled woollen fabric, used for uniforms and suits.

clue.text: Drinks interrupted by correspondence from gospellers

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing placed in its middle

parts.note: ales are drinks
post is mail or correspondence

explanation.surface: A drinking session is cut short by letters from evangelists.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were Jesus's followers who spread the gospel; gospellers are preachers of it.
